svg.title: Spark + Comet: Arrow batches from source file to target file
svg.text: With Comet the data stays an Arrow batch from file to file

g.text: Rust, once per Arrow batch
files and JVM work, once per file or per job
Iceberg table lineitem: Parquet data files
Map stage · one native plan per task
CometIcebergNativeScan · iceberg-rust reader
Rust
decodes Parquet into Arrow arrays (up to 8,192 rows) and applies the WHERE filter
CometFilter → CometProject
Rust
whole columns: boolean mask, filter kernel, Decimal128 multiply
CometHashAggregate (partial) · DataFusion AggregateExec
Rust
per batch: hash the key column, map the hashes to group indices,
update the Decimal128 sums and the counts for the whole batch
CometExchange · native shuffle writer
Rust
per batch: Murmur3 + pmod → partition ids; gather each partition's rows
write each block as an lz4-compressed Arrow IPC stream
Shuffle files on local disk
same layout as Spark: one data file + one index file per map task; Arrow IPC blocks
Reduce stage · one task per shuffle partition
Native shuffle read
Rust
decompress and decode the Arrow IPC blocks in Rust (direct read, no Arrow FFI hop)
CometHashAggregate (final)
Rust
per batch: merge the partial sums and counts by group
CometIcebergWrite · iceberg-rust Parquet writer
Rust
Arrow arrays straight into column pages, zstd; no rows anywhere
IcebergCommit · iceberg-java on the driver
JVM
adds the new data files to a new snapshot of the table
Iceberg table order_revenue: new data files
Shown with spark.comet.write.iceberg.enabled=true. With the default (false), CometColumnarToRow and
AppendData with iceberg-java's row writer take the place of CometIcebergWrite and IcebergCommit.
